name: Myriophyllum
look_here_first: Find whorled featherlike submerged leaves, then inspect emergent flowering bracts.
shared_genus_characters: Aquatic herbs with finely divided submerged leaves and tiny flowers in upper axils.

species_comparison_matrix.aquaticum: Dioecious; North American populations are pistillate
Whorls commonly 4–6(–8); submerged leaves usually 25–70 mm, with about 14–36 threadlike segments.
species_comparison_matrix.heterophyllum: Whorls commonly 4–5; submerged leaves typically 20–40 mm with about 5–12 segment pairs.
species_comparison_matrix.caution: These ranges overlap; emergent bracts are more diagnostic.

overlap_and_cautions: Submerged foliage alone is insufficient for confident species ID.
M. aquaticum is introduced and not yet a canonical learner species; M. heterophyllum has provisional target-zone status.
The family module's common male-upper/female-lower cue does not apply to dioecious M. aquaticum; use the species-specific reproductive architecture.
lookalikes: Ceratophyllum has forked rather than pinnate leaves.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched side-by-side emergent shoots with leaf bases and bract margins; label featherlike divisions vs broad serrulate edges.
Same-scale submerged nodes, whorl count, central leaf axis and lateral segments.
Flowering-node macro showing pistillate flower in M. aquaticum and hermaphroditic/sex arrangement in M. heterophyllum when available.
Scaled fruit and mericarp views where fruit is present; do not treat lack of fruit in female-only populations as an ID key.

project_scope.installer_dependency: M. aquaticum source-pool approved but not canonical; Approved Taxa Installer owns species-card creation.
project_scope.range_note: M. heterophyllum target-zone status remains PROVISIONAL; M. aquaticum is introduced. No range decisions changed.

decision_sequence: Identify whorled, pinnately divided submerged leaves with a central leaf axis; inspect intact nodes rather than loose fragments.
Follow a stem above water. Feathery divided emergent bracts favor M. aquaticum; broader sharply serrulate bracts favor M. heterophyllum.

If flowers are visible, distinguish dioecious pistillate M. aquaticum shoots from the hermaphroditic or occasionally monoecious M. heterophyllum; do not apply a male-above/female-below rule to all watermilfoils.
Use mature fruit lobe depth as supporting evidence when fruit exists. If only submerged fragments are available, leave at Myriophyllum sp.
